destructive-minded
the same as Homeric ὀλοόφρων [destructive-minded], and the mind is destructive, or one who plots destruction for someone.
Thus Valckenaer for δουλόφρονες [slavish-minded].

therefore, then

a syllogistic particle, which serves for drawing an inference from what precedes, like Latin ergo, igitur, in positive or interrogative sentences. Not rarely it serves not so much for argumentation properly so called as for continuing and connecting the discourse, like Latin igitur.
Frequently after the interrogative pronoun τίς [who?].
And after interrogative particles
After μῶν [surely not?]
οὖν [then] joined with other particles. ἀλλ᾽ οὖν [but then].
γὰρ οὖν [for then].
δ᾽ οὖν [but then].
εἴτ᾽ οὖν [or then] dialectically serves for inferring the opposite.
μὲν οὖν [indeed then].
μήτ᾽ οὖν [neither then].
οὔτ᾽ οὖν [nor then].
περ οὖν [indeed then].
thus corruptly for οὐκέτ᾽ ἂν [no longer would], which has been restored from the apograph.
thus Blomfield for ή [or]
